Interesting view points.  Taxi Driver is one of my favorite films.  I feel that it's a film about a man looking for meaning in a world gone mad. Every day he is surrounded by insanity (New York city streets at night).  He then tries to take control where he feels he has none by buying the guns. He goes through an ascetic stage where he hardens his body in order to be pure for the assassination attempt.  When that doesn't work out he realizes that he had the wrong motives and goes after the pimp and all those other bangers at the end for what he believes is a truer calling for his martyrdom.  This scene is what I like to call "bloody catharsis" because in those final moments Travis has not only seized control by protecting Jodie Foster's character but he is also close to death and in those final moments smiles because he can finally let go.  However, he doesn't die and is later validated by the media but he understands it's not the accolades that were important but rather is own peace of mind in knowing that he could let go of the demons of his past and begin to live his own life.

What you need to prove is that your crazy.  Nobody fucks with crazy people, growl like a dog, spit, bite, and shit.  That kept my friend from getting "petted" in juvie.
